title: Review bypassed Spring transaction advice
why: A direct same-class call bypasses the target method's requested transactional proxy advice. An existing caller transaction may remain active, so this does not imply that all transactional behavior disappears.
suggestion: Review the intended transaction boundary and settings; when target advice is required, invoke it through a separate managed bean or another deliberate interception boundary.
limitations: Advisory, count-mode by default: method- or class-level canonical Transactional bindings use explicit imports, wildcard imports, or fully qualified names. Top-level nonabstract managed classes require canonical stereotypes or an unambiguous Bean return type. Direct same-owner calls provide structural evidence, not proof that a new transaction is required.

Findings use the primary annotation location and group target calls in code_flow. Analysis abstains on extends/implements, same-name overloads, varargs or private/static targets, explicit generic receiver calls, other receivers, lambdas, and anonymous/local/inner classes. Matching caller settings for REQUIRED, SUPPORTS, MANDATORY, NEVER, and NOT_SUPPORTED are excluded; REQUIRES_NEW and NESTED still require their own interception boundary.

Explicit per-module EnableTransactionManagement AspectJ mode suppresses this proxy-only rule. Dynamic configuration, custom meta-annotations, external type resolution, unresolved Maven properties or remote parents, and non-Java source are not resolved.
